Subject: Invoice currency mismatch and VAT ID evidence for reverse charge

Hi Marta / Accounts team,

Quick note on invoice INV-9082 that came through this morning. Two items we need to resolve before collection:

1) Currency discrepancy: The invoice was issued in GBP but our contract is EUR-denominated. The invoice shows a conversion that increases the total by ~2.7% compared to the exchange rate on the invoice date. Can you confirm whether OrbitalTech prefers us to reissue in EUR or accept the GBP invoice and book the FX delta as a separate credit?

2) VAT / reverse-charge: Your AR team included a VAT number on the remit details but we need official VAT residency evidence to apply the EU reverse-charge. Please attach a VAT registration certificate or a portal screenshot that shows the entity and VAT ID. We can’t treat the line items as reverse-charged until we have that.

I’ve attached a short template (see also our evidence checklist) — if you can send the VAT cert and confirm the currency preference, we’ll proceed to either reissue or issue a corrective credit and schedule payment.

Attachments: 2026-01-15_orbitaltech_vat_certificate.pdf (placeholder)

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: RE: Invoice currency mismatch and VAT ID evidence for reverse charge

Thanks — good catch. A few quick internal notes and proposal:

Summary of facts:
- External provided VAT cert (attached in thread): OrbitalTech Ltd, valid EU VAT ID.
- Original invoice INV-9082 issued in GBP; contract / PO states EUR pricing. FX delta ~+2.7%.

Recommended approach (finance_billing):
1) Reissue invoice in EUR (new invoice: Redwood-9082-EUR). Include explicit reverse-charge wording on the invoice: "Reverse charge — customer liable for VAT under Article 194" and the buyer VAT ID in the header.
2) Issue a small credit note to account for the GBP/EUR FX difference so that OrbitalTech is not materially impacted by the conversion. The credit will reference INV-9082 and be net (no VAT).
3) Collection timing: once reissued invoice & credit note are in GB/DR system, AR can accept payment within standard terms. Recommend asking customer to confirm payment date (Tom) and to provide the bank remittance once payment is sent.

Risk/controls:
- We must keep the VAT evidence file in the audit folder (Irene, please upload to secure Drive folder and note the HubSpot record).
- If Finance/legal want to escrow anything, flag now — otherwise this is routine.

Irene/Ben — can you confirm you’re ok with steps 1–3? If yes I’ll draft the reissued invoice and credit note and put them into the queue for signature.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Subject: RE: Invoice currency mismatch and VAT ID evidence for reverse charge

Hi Marta / Tom —

Thanks for the certificate and the quick turnaround. We’ve agreed internally to proceed as follows:

• We will reissue the invoice in EUR (new invoice number: Redwood-9082-EUR). The invoice will carry an explicit reverse-charge statement and reference your VAT ID.

• We will issue a separate credit note to correct the GBP -> EUR conversion delta (Credit note: Redwood-CN-9082). That credit will be net of VAT.

• Expected timeline: reissued invoice + credit note will be uploaded to the Drive folder and sent to your AR inbox by end of day tomorrow (21 Jan). Once you confirm receipt and acceptance, please proceed with payment under the original terms.

• Audit trail: I’ve uploaded the provided VAT registration to our secure evidence folder and linked it to HubSpot record HS-54219.

Attachments: 2026-01-20_Redwood_reissued_invoice_9082.pdf (stub), 2026-01-20_Redwood_credit_note_9082.pdf (stub)

If you’d prefer we simply accept the original GBP invoice and issue an FX-only credit instead, we can do that — but reissue in EUR is cleaner for both accounting teams. Please confirm which you prefer; otherwise we’ll proceed with the EUR reissue.

Best regards,
